overview_raw: The Sheet Metal Foundation teaches students how to fabricate, assemble, alter and install a variety of sheet metal products. Typical jobs performed by a sheet metal worker include HVAC (Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning) ductwork, industrial sheet metal work, and residential sheet metal work. Delivery: in person. See details . Note: Next program offering is September TBD 2026. They also work on hospital and kitchen equipment (stainless steel), industrial exhaust systems, industrial sheet metal work, and roofing and flashing (copper, aluminum, stainless steel and galvanized iron). BCIT Sheet Metal—hands-on training for industry The program Basic theory and related information, along with hands-on shop practice enable students to become competent in fabricating basic sheet metal products. Sheet metal workers must be able to work at heights. Good physical condition is necessary. Potential students with medical or physical difficulties should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview (telephone interview if out of town) with the institute’s rehabilitation specialist, 604-451-6963. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. courses.course_overview_raw: ​Being employed in the sheet metal trade means you could be working in a shop environment or working on a job site. Some of the responsibilities of sheet metal workers include reading blueprints and specifications, layout and fabrication, installation of sheet metal systems, altering existing systems, and welding. The course includes topics such as fabrication, assembly, and installation of a variety of sheet metal products. A special emphasis is placed on the fabrication and installation of air and material handling systems. In addition, stainless steel fabrication and installation of components for such environments as hospitals and commercial kitchens and medical research facilities is also covered in the course. Architectural components, roofing and flashing (copper, aluminum, stainless steel and galvanized iron) are also within the scope of the Sheet Metal Worker program. This course outline has been developed to comply with the Industry Training Authority (ITA) Program Outline for Sheet Metal Worker Level 1 as published January 2018. Prerequisite(s): Acceptance to the Sheet Metal Foundation Program.
